quote_original: Then the scene dissolved and I awoke.
context_before: Once out of my skull, an unearthly wind caused my head – as well as the house – to rattle. Looking for the cause, my attention was diverted for a few seconds. And when I looked back, my body was gone and in its place were my three brothers. One was sitting where the head had been, while the other two were sitting at the feet. Disturbed by the sound, one rose and moved in the direction of the wind. Looking down, he said: “Why, it’s Neville’s baby.” The other two questioned his words, saying: “How can Neville have a baby?” Without arguing the point, my brother reached down, picked up a baby wrapped in swaddling clothes, and placed it on the bed. Then I, as though having rehearsed the drama in eternity, took the babe in my arms and said: “How is my sweetheart?” as the child broke into a heavenly smile.

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: So you see: a child is not born.
context_before: We are told that each individual is born again through the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead. I, an individual, have found him of whom Moses and the law and the prophets wrote, for when I awoke in that tomb no one else was there. I recognized that tomb to be my skull and when I came out from its base I found the sign of my spiritual birth as a babe wrapped in swaddling clothes, lying on the floor. The word translated “manger” means “floor; the lowest point in the area”.
context_after: The child is only a sign of your individual spiritual birth.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Follow Me (1968-11-11).

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: I was awed at this experience.
context_before: t God was not only crucified upon me, but was buried within me. That I carried in my body the death of Jesus, that his life might be made alive in me.
context_after: Knowing all of the things I had done and was still capable of doing, I wondered how I could be the Christ of scripture. Yet I have searched scripture and cannot find any other explanation. I now share with you what I have experienced, for everything recorded there as an event in the life of one called Jesus Christ has unfolded in me.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Follow Me (1968-11-11).

quote_original: That you will believe my experiences.
context_before: This is my story. It is my hope that you will follow me.
context_after: If I tell you earthly things and you do not believe me, how can I expect you to believe the heavenly things I share with you?
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Follow Me (1968-11-11).

quote_original: My friend also shared this experience.
context_before: in himself. Although humanity appears to be independent, with life in themselves, their life is but an activity of imagination, for that is what I AM!
context_after: One night in dream she was in a classroom listening to a woman teach the law. Claiming to believe and practice the law, the woman began to rant and rave against Neville, claiming he was insane, as she did not believe in the promise. The lady then asked the teacher: “Do you believe that imagining creates reality?” and when the woman replied, Yes, the lady asked: “How would you feel right now if you began to imagine you were God?” With that the teacher screamed: “”You should be in the same institution with Neville!”
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Follow Me (1968-11-11).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-11-11 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: And if you did would you become God?
context_before: It is easy to mouth the words: imagining creates reality, but are you willing to imagine you are God?
context_after: At that thought a line was drawn, so she does not really believe that imagining creates reality. She is willing to believe that she can imagine things are better than they seem to be, but to believe she is God is an insane thought.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Follow Me (1968-11-11).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-11-11 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: I am not theorizing or speculating.
context_before: Paul asks the question: “Do you not know you are the temple of the living God and the spirit of God dwells in you?” (1 Cor. 3:16) If the curtain of that temple is torn from top to bottom, it has to be you! The spirit who ascends is he who is buried in you, and will rise in the same manner as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness. So when I ask you to follow me, I mean it literally, for I am telling you what I know from experience.
context_after: Redemption is a very personal experience that takes place in the individual you.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Follow Me (1968-11-11).

author: Neville Goddard
rights_note: Delivered in public spoken lecture on 1968-11-11 in the United States; public domain under 1909 US Copyright Act.
quote_original: That is because they do not know the mystery of Christ.
context_before: There are those who believe they are reborn by changing their attitude and giving more money to the church.
context_after: My visions would frighten them and they would call me mad; yet I am telling the truth which I know from experience. I am not trying to share some workable philosophy of life.
selection_note: Verbatim lecture excerpt from Follow Me (1968-11-11).

author: Neville Goddard

quote_original: Every man’s words are his judge.
context_before: the veil is removed from your spiritual eyes, and you will realize humanity is doing what must be done in order for God’s image to be formed in them.
context_after: Believe me and follow me into an entirely different sphere known as the kingdom of God.
